issues.main_description_html:
Video.Project.15.mp4

What this covers

Stitching now works as a batch: pick your fisheye photos, they get grouped automatically into sets (4 photos per panorama by default), and each group runs through the stitching pipeline on its own — progress shown per group, cancel one without stopping the rest, results shown as soon as ready.

New: fixing a bad seam by hand

Sometimes two photos won't line up automatically — usually a plain wall or a repeating pattern like wallpaper, where the software can't tell one spot from another. For those cases, every panorama now has a "Manual control points" button.

Opening it shows the seam (the two overlapping photos) side by side. Click the same real-world spot in both — a corner, a light fixture, anything recognizable — a few times per seam, then save. The next stitch uses those points to line the seam up correctly.

A few things that go with it:

  • If the automatic matching got a seam completely wrong (not just sparse), there's a toggle to ignore its points and use only what you marked.
  • Panoramas that clearly need this get a warning badge, easy to spot in a big batch.
  • A group that already has points marked shows a small counter.
  • Clear all marked points on a group and start over anytime.

Everyday flow

  1. Add photos to the queue.
  2. Start stitching — each group processes in order.
  3. Check results. If a panorama looks wrong, open "Manual control points," mark a few spots on the bad seam, hit "Save and stitch again."
  4. Repeat only for groups that need it.

COMPARE WITH FINDER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-06.at.15.03.58.mov

Problem

PR #143 fixes the four problems raised in the team feedback — large folders being slow, files that cannot be deleted or renamed, having to click Reload after every external change, and NAS drives mounted over the network. All four share one root: network volumes were treated exactly like local disks.

It passes the static gates only — cargo check, cargo clippy, cargo fmt, pnpm typecheck, and cargo test --lib commands::files (8 passed, including a new UNC normalisation test). The thing it actually fixes has not been exercised. A real SMB share, a Windows machine and a second machine writing into the same folder are not reachable from a test runner, and the Win32 call sites (GetDriveTypeW, GetLogicalDrives) are cross-compile verified only — they have never been executed.

What needs hands on it:

  • UNC paths — normalize_target_ext used to squeeze the leading // of \\NAS\share\photos into one slash and then strip it, leaving the relative NAS/share/photos. Any share not mapped to a drive letter simply would not open. Only a real share proves the round-trip: opening it, navigating into subfolders, and going back up.
  • Polling watcher — network folders now watch through notify::PollWatcher at a 5 s interval, because macOS FSEvents reports nothing at all for an SMB mount. Whether 5 s feels right, and whether polling a large folder costs anything noticeable, is a judgement only real use makes.
  • File locking — thumbnail prewarming is capped at 200 images and skipped entirely on network volumes, and watcher::release_dir now drops the watcher before a destructive op touches the watched folder. Both are Windows handle-semantics fixes (std::fs opens without FILE_SHARE_DELETE); on macOS they cannot fail the way they did for the user.
  • Large folders — the directory scan moved to the blocking pool and now reuses the metadata read_dir already returned instead of stat'ing every entry twice. Over SMB that removes one round-trip per file; the size of the win only shows on a real share.

What to do

Run on Windows, against an actual NAS share, on a real build (pnpm tauri dev or a release build — note which). Prepare a folder of a few thousand images on the share, a second machine (or a second Explorer window) able to write into it, and files you do not mind sending to the recycle bin. Work on copies.

  • N1 — UNC path opens. Type \\NAS\share into the path bar. The folder lists. Navigate into a subfolder and back out. (Before this PR: nothing opened at all.)
  • N2 — mapped drive opens. Same share mapped to a drive letter (e.g. Z:). Still lists, still navigates.
  • N3 — external add. With the share open in the app, create a file in that folder from the other machine. It appears in the grid within ~5 s, without touching Reload.
  • N4 — external delete. Delete a file from the other machine. It disappears from the grid within ~5 s, without Reload.
  • N5 — local folder unaffected. Repeat N3/N4 on a local folder. Changes still appear immediately (native watcher, not the poller) — this is the regression check on the watcher split.
  • N6 — delete during load. Open a large folder and delete a file from the grid while it is still filling in. The delete succeeds; no "file in use".
  • N7 — rename the open folder. Rename the folder currently open in the app, from the app and again from Explorer. Both succeed. (This is the watcher directory-handle fix.)
  • N8 — delete the open folder. Same, with delete to recycle bin.
  • N9 — large folder responsiveness. Open a folder with a few thousand images on the share. The window stays responsive while it lists; note roughly how long the listing takes so we have a number to compare against.
  • N10 — "My Computer" with a dead mapped drive. Disconnect the NAS but leave the drive letter mapped, then open "My Computer". It lists at once instead of hanging for tens of seconds.

Expected

Every row passes, or fails into its own issue.

N6, N7 and N8 are the blocker rows — they are the "locking files" complaint the user actually reported. If any of them still fails, that is the finding worth chasing before the rest.

Note

Also worth watching while testing: thumbnails on a network folder are now fetched only for the cards the grid displays, so scrolling fast through a NAS folder should show placeholders filling in behind you. That is intended. Thumbnails failing to appear at all, or a folder that never finishes listing, is not.

A mac pass on an SMB mount is useful as a second data point (N1 as /Volumes/..., N3–N5, N9), but the locking rows are Windows-only by nature.

This is the gate before PR #143 merges.

issues.display_title: Issue #168: get-raw-exif and get-file-on-folder still run on the main thread, freezing the window on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.25.12.mov

Two commands still do their filesystem work on the main thread, so the window is frozen for the whole duration. On a local disk this is invisible; on a network share every operation is a round-trip and the freeze becomes seconds.

Why a sync command freezes the window

A #[tauri::command] pub fn (no async) runs on the main thread, for as long as it takes. Traced through the dependency versions this repo pins:

  • tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.3/src/lib.rs:5197 — webview custom protocols are registered with wry's with_asynchronous_custom_protocol. "Asynchronous" only defers the response; the handler closure still fires on the UI thread.
  • tauri-2.11.3/src/manager/webview.rs:282 — the ipc scheme goes through that same registration.
  • tauri-2.11.3/src/ipc/protocol.rs:38 — get calls webview.on_message(...) inline, which calls manager.run_invoke_handler(invoke) inline. No spawn anywhere on the path.
  • tauri-macros-2.6.3/src/command/wrapper.rs:429 — body_blocking expands to let result = $path(args);, called inline.

This is the same class of bug as the asset:// protocol handler fixed in 6aadddb, just entering through the IPC path instead.

Remaining commands

1. get-raw-exif — src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs:605

Opens the same file five times, all on the main thread:

  • path.exists() — 1 round-trip
  • metadata_for(path_str) — fs::metadata, imagesize::size, read_exif, jpeg_sof (reads 256 KB) = 4 more

Single file, so roughly 15 ms on a wired NAS and up to ~150 ms over WiFi. Noticeable stutter each time the raw-EXIF popup opens, not fatal.

Callers: src/renderer/features/preview/RawExifPopup.tsx:61, src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Stitching/hooks/useStitching.ts:275.

2. get-file-on-folder — src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs:203

read_dir plus a p.is_file() per entry, serial, on the main thread. Structurally identical to the load-files problem fixed in 6aadddb — this command just never got the same treatment.

Worse than get-raw-exif because it scales with folder size, and every caller runs it over a folder the user picked for a batch job:

  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/CubeToEquirectangular/ProgressList.tsx:174
  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/MinifyJpg/hooks/useMinifyJpgAddToQueue.ts:77
  • src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Enfuse/hooks/useEnfuseQueue.ts:225

Fix

Same mechanical shape already applied to the batch commands on fix/nas:

  • pub fn → pub async fn
  • body into tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking
  • par_iter where there is a per-entry loop (get-file-on-folder)

For get-raw-exif there is a second, optional win: jpeg_sof already reads 256 KB, which is enough to satisfy imagesize and the EXIF parser too. Folding the four opens into one would cut it to a single round-trip — worth measuring after the spawn_blocking change, not before.

Guard against regressions

New commands that touch the filesystem should default to pub async fn + spawn_blocking. A sync command is only safe when it does no I/O at all (generate_uuid, is_windows) or exactly one stat on a path that is always local.

Deliberately out of scope — single-file stat, not loops, so they cannot freeze for more than one round-trip:

  • room_staging_check_overwrite (src-tauri/src/commands/room_staging.rs:649)
  • virtual_staging_2d_check_overwrite (src-tauri/src/commands/virtual_staging_2d.rs:162)
  • get_file_stats, create_folder, rename_image, rename_file_or_folder, check_directory_exists
  • resolve_path_to_absolute (src-tauri/src/commands/system.rs:66) — up to 3 stats plus a canonicalize, which resolves per path component over SMB. Upper bound worth remembering if path resolution ever shows up in a profile.

issues.display_title: Issue #160: Copy and move into a mounted USB or network volume silently do nothing
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.45.16.mov

What happens

In the File Manager, copying or moving files into a panel pointed at a mounted volume (USB stick, or an SMB/network share) does nothing at all. No file appears at the destination, and no error or toast is shown — the operation looks like it was ignored.

Root cause: resolve_dest in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs anchored the renderer's display-relative currentDirectory at $HOME unconditionally. Mounted volumes are anchored at the volumes root instead (/Volumes on macOS, /media on Linux), so a destination of sambashare resolved to $HOME/sambashare, which does not exist, and the command returned error: "Destination folder does not exist.".

The listing side already handles both anchors — normalize_target_ext in src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs falls back to the volumes root when the home anchor does not exist. Copy and move never got that treatment, so browsing a volume worked while writing to it did not.

Second defect, which is why it failed silently: copySources and moveSources in src/renderer/features/fileManager/hooks/useFileOperations.ts only report a failure from .catch(). The command resolves with error set rather than rejecting, so the error branch never ran.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) or plug in a USB drive.
  2. Open File Manager and point the right panel at the volume (My Computer → the volume, e.g. sambashare).
  3. Select any file in the left panel (e.g. under Documents) and press Copy.
  4. Nothing arrives in the right panel. No toast, no error, no entry.

Copying into an ordinary folder under the home directory works, which is what makes this look like a NAS/permissions problem rather than a path bug. Verified it is not permissions: cp, mkdir, xattr and cp -p all succeed against the same mount from a terminal.

Goal

  1. Copy and move into a mounted USB or network volume write the files to the volume.
  2. Copy and move into ordinary home-relative folders behave exactly as before.
  3. Same-name conflicts still route through the existing overwrite modal.
  4. A copy or move that fails surfaces a toast instead of failing silently.

issues.display_title: Issue #161: File Manager freezes during copy, move and delete, with no progress indication
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.45.16.mov

What happens

Copying a large file to a network share — or deleting on one — freezes the entire window for the whole operation. No repaint, no input, no indication that anything is happening. On a Tailscale-backed SMB mount measured at ~1.1 MB/s, a 72 MB panorama is roughly 65 seconds of a dead window, which is indistinguishable from a hang.

Root cause: copy_sources, move_sources and delete_sources in src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs are declared #[tauri::command] without async. Tauri runs a non-async command on the main thread, so the transfer blocks the event loop. This is a real freeze, not just a missing spinner. remove_images in the same file already uses the correct async fn + injected AppHandle signature.

Separately, none of the three report progress. The shared ProgressModal (src/renderer/components/modals/ProgressModal.tsx) already exists but is only driven by rotate, duplicate and image-centering.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a slow network share (SMB over a VPN/tunnel makes it obvious).
  2. Open File Manager and point one panel at the share.
  3. Copy a file of 50 MB or more into it.
  4. The window stops responding until the copy finishes. Nothing on screen indicates progress or that the app is still alive.

Deleting several files on the same share shows the same freeze.

Goal

  1. The window stays responsive during copy, move and delete.
  2. A progress modal appears for operations slow enough to be noticeable, and always closes when the operation ends — including on failure. An operation that opens a modal and never closes it is worse than no modal.
  3. Copy and move progress is measured in bytes, not files. A File Manager selection is usually a handful of very large panoramas — often exactly one — so a file counter would sit at 0% for the entire transfer and then jump to 100%.
  4. Delete reports file counts instead: trashing is a rename, so its cost scales with entry count, not size.
  5. Fast local operations do not flash a modal on screen.
  6. The existing rotate / duplicate / image-centering progress behaviour is unchanged.

issues.display_title: Issue #159: USB/network drive badge background does not fully wrap the icon in File Manager
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

What happens

In the File Manager, folders detected as removable (USB) or network drives get a small badge overlay in the top-left corner of the folder thumbnail. The badge's blue background does not fully wrap the icon — the right side of the glyph overflows the blue box, so the badge looks clipped and the padding reads as uneven.

Root cause: Font Awesome 7's base rule sets width: var(--fa-width, 1.25em) on the icon element. Combined with Tailwind's box-sizing: border-box preflight, that 1.25em is the total width including padding, so the padding consumes the content box and the glyph (whose advance is a full 1.25em) overflows to the right.

Complicating factor: @fortawesome/fontawesome-pro/css/all.min.css is imported after tailwindcss in src/renderer/index.css, so Font Awesome's rules win the cascade against equal-specificity Tailwind utilities — w-auto, inline-flex, and leading-none have no effect on these badges.

Affected element: src/renderer/components/shared/browse/ItemThumb.tsx → FolderThumb, both the fa-usb badge (removable drive / item.external) and the fa-network-wired badge (network drive).

How to reproduce

  1. Plug in a USB drive (or mount a network share).
  2. Open File Manager and browse to My Computer.
  3. Look at the folder thumbnail for the USB volume — e.g. sambashare, Macintosh HD - Data.
  4. The blue badge in the top-left corner does not fully cover the USB icon; the right edge of the icon sits outside the blue box.

Goal

  1. The blue badge background fully encloses the USB icon, with visually equal padding on all four sides.
  2. The same fix applies to the network-drive badge, which shares the identical styling bug.
  3. The badge stays correct at the different thumbnail sizes produced by the File Manager zoom slider.
  4. The fix does not rely on !important overrides — it works with the existing Tailwind → Font Awesome import order.

issues.display_title: Issue #162: Video buffering label is hardcoded English instead of going through i18n
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

What happens

The spinner shown while a video buffers carries a literal English string, so it stays English in all 18 locales.

src/renderer/features/preview/VideoControlsOverlay.tsx:70

<Spinner size="lg" color="white" label="Buffering..." />

Every other user-facing string in the app goes through t(...) with src/locales/*.json (base en.json).

This became more visible after the viewer loading work on fix/nas: the image loading overlay is deliberately not raised for video, because this buffering overlay already covers the video case (including re-buffering and seeking mid-playback). That makes this label the only loading text a video ever shows.

How to reproduce

  1. Switch the app language to anything other than English (flag menu, top right).
  2. Open a folder containing a video — ideally on a network share or another slow location, so the buffering state lasts long enough to read.
  3. Click the video.
  4. The spinner overlay reads "Buffering..." in English while every other label around it is translated.

Goal

The buffering label is translated like every other user-facing string.

  • Add a key (e.g. t_video_buffering) to all 18 files in src/locales/, base text in en.json.
  • Swap the literal for t(...) in VideoControlsOverlay.tsx.
  • pnpm i18n:check stays at its current baseline.

issues.display_title: Issue #163: gtimg protocol buffers the whole file in memory when no Range header is sent
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.54.07.mov

What happens

The gtimg URI scheme (added on fix/nas, commit 6aadddb) serves local images and video off the blocking pool, so the main thread is never blocked by a network-share read.

A request that arrives without a Range header is answered by reading the entire file into a Vec<u8>:

src-tauri/src/lib.rs — see the ponytail: note above gtimg_response (~line 140)

For images this is correct and intended: a panorama is decoded as one buffer anyway. It is a known ceiling for video only — a range-less request for a multi-gigabyte video would spike memory by the full size of the file.

How to reproduce

Not reachable through normal use — media elements send Range, which is why this was left as-is. To force it:

  1. Open a folder with a large video file.
  2. In the webview devtools console, fetch the video URL directly with no range header: 
    fetch(document.querySelector('video').src).then(r => r.arrayBuffer())
  3. Watch the app process in Activity Monitor — resident memory climbs by roughly the size of the file, and stays up until the buffer is dropped.

Compare against normal playback, where the same file is served in ~1MB slices and memory stays flat.

Goal

Serving a large file cannot spike memory by its full size, whatever the client asks for.

Only worth doing if a real client is observed issuing a range-less request for a large video — measure before building anything. Then either:

  • Stream the body instead of buffering it, or
  • Refuse range-less requests above a size threshold so the element retries with ranges.

issues.display_title: Issue #164: gtimg protocol answers multi-range requests with 416 instead of multipart/byteranges
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.54.07.mov

What happens

The gtimg range parser handles a single range only. A header requesting several (Range: bytes=0-99,200-299) is rejected, and the caller answers 416 Range Not Satisfiable.

src-tauri/src/lib.rs — gtimg_range, see the ponytail: note (~line 99)

This was a deliberate simplification: serving multiple ranges requires building a multipart/byteranges body with boundary separators, and no browser media element is known to request one. A 416 makes clients retry with a single range, so playback still works today.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder with any image or video.
  2. In the webview devtools console, request the media URL with a multi-range header: 
    fetch(document.querySelector('video, img').src, {
  headers: { Range: 'bytes=0-99,200-299' }
}).then(r => console.log(r.status)) // 416
  3. The response is 416 with Content-Range: bytes */<len> and an empty body, instead of a 206 carrying a multipart/byteranges payload.

Also covered as a unit test — gtimg_range_parses_the_forms_media_elements_send in src-tauri/src/lib.rs asserts the multi-range case returns None:

cargo test --lib gtimg

Goal

Multi-range requests are served properly, if something is ever observed sending one.

  • Build the multipart/byteranges response. Tauri own src/protocol/asset.rs has a reference implementation.
  • Update gtimg_range_parses_the_forms_media_elements_send rather than deleting it — the multi-range assertion needs to change, not disappear.
  • If nothing sends multi-range requests, leaving the 416 is the correct outcome and this can be closed as wontfix.

issues.display_title: Issue #165: Each thumbnail stats its source file twice, doubling round-trips on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.56.33.mov

What happens

Rendering one grid thumbnail issues two separate metadata() calls against the same source file:

  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs:325 — thumb_path checks src.is_file()
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs:202 — cache_file then calls mtime_ms(src) to build the cache key

On local disk both are effectively free. On an SMB/NFS share each one is a network round-trip, so every thumbnail pays two where one would do — on top of reading the source file itself.

Found while fixing the NAS freezes on fix/nas (commit 6aadddb) and deliberately left out of that change, which addressed the larger causes first: the main-thread asset-protocol read, the serial directory scan, and the full-folder thumbnail prewarm.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) and put a folder of images on it.
  2. Clear the thumbnail cache (Settings → cache, or delete the thumbnail dir) so every thumbnail is a cache miss.
  3. Trace filesystem calls while opening the folder: 
    sudo fs_usage -w -f filesys | grep -i '<your-share-name>'
  4. Each image shows two stat/getattr calls before its content read, rather than one.

The doubled stats also occur on cache hits, where they are the entire cost of the call — thumb_path stats twice and then returns the cached path without reading the source at all.

Goal

One stat per thumbnail instead of two.

  • Take one fs::metadata in thumb_path and pass the resulting mtime into cache_file, so the cache key is built from the stat already performed.
  • Keep the cache key semantics identical — it is hash(path + mtime + w/h/q + orient), and changing it silently invalidates every cached thumbnail.

issues.display_title: Issue #166: load-files shows nothing until the entire directory has been scanned
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.56.33.mov

What happens

msg_load_files builds the complete listing before emitting anything, so the browse grid stays on the previous folder until the last entry has been stat-ed.

src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs — msg_load_files

On fix/nas (commit 6aadddb) this was made much faster: the per-entry metadata() calls now run in parallel via rayon on the blocking pool, and a load-files-start event raises the grid progress bar so the wait is at least visible. But the model is still all-or-nothing — a very large directory on a slow share still shows a progress bar and nothing else for the whole scan.

The progress bar is also necessarily indeterminate, because the entry count is unknown until read_dir finishes. Streaming would make a real 120 / 450 counter possible.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a network share (SMB) with a directory holding several hundred files.
  2. Open the app, navigate to a different folder first so there is a visible previous listing.
  3. Open the large folder.
  4. The progress bar appears immediately, but the grid keeps showing the old folder contents for the whole scan, then swaps to the complete new listing in one step. Nothing appears incrementally, and the bar gives no sense of how far along it is.

Contrast with recursive search in the same app, which streams results in as they are found.

Goal

The grid fills in progressively instead of waiting for the whole directory, and the progress bar can show a real count.

  • Emit the listing in chunks the way msg_search_recursive already does in the same file — see SEARCH_CHUNK_SIZE / SEARCH_CHUNK_MS (~line 719) and its search-start → search-results → search-done sequence.
  • This touches the renderer: src/renderer/components/core/ipcHandlers/files.ts currently handles load-files as a single payload that replaces the whole list, and sorting happens backend-side across the full set — chunked delivery has to preserve the folders-first ordering.
  • Measure first. After the parallel scan landed, this may no longer be worth the renderer churn.

issues.display_title: Issue #169: 360 video on a network share offers no 360 or fisheye mode
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.54.07.mov

What happens

Selecting a 360 video on a network share leaves the viewer with only the flat mode button. The 360 and fisheye buttons never appear, so an equirectangular video can only be watched as a stretched rectangle. The same file on a local disk offers all three.

The buttons are gated on isPanorama, which for a video comes from the file's ProjectionType:

src/renderer/features/preview/MainViewerToolbarLeft.tsx:61 → src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/usePanoramaViewMode.ts:83 → src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/useViewerImage.ts:42

const pathA = displayMetadata.SourceFile?...;
const pathB = displayedFile?.path?...;
if (pathA !== pathB) return false;
return displayMetadata.ProjectionType === 'equirectangular';

The tag itself reads fine over SMB — the bundled exiftool returns "ProjectionType": "equirectangular" for a file on a mounted share in under a second. What fails is that the reply never reaches displayMetadata.

Root cause: get-metadata replies are not correlated with their request

src/renderer/hooks/useSelectDisplay.tsx sends the request and then subscribes to the shared message bus:

ipc.sendMessage({ type: 'get-metadata', data: { file: filePath } });
const unregisterListener = ipc.onRendererMessage((raw) => {
  if (event.type === 'get-metadata') {
    if (event.data?.result) { dispatch(setDisplayMetadata(metadata)); }
    ...
    unregisterListener();   // fires for ANY get-metadata reply
  }
});

The bus is a broadcast: every listener sees every reply, and the reply carries no indication of which file it belongs to (src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs, msg_get_metadata, emits data: { result } only). So with two requests in flight:

  1. User selects image A → request A sent, listener A registered.
  2. User selects video B before A has replied → request B sent, listener B registered.
  3. A's reply arrives. Both listeners take it: displayMetadata is set to A's metadata, and both listeners unregister.
  4. B's reply arrives with nothing listening. It is dropped.

displayMetadata.SourceFile is now image A while displayedFile.path is video B, the guard above returns false, and the viewer decides the video is not a panorama.

This is not a narrow race on a network share, it is the normal case. Reading an image's metadata is six separate opens of the file — metadata_for, read_exif, read_xmp_gpano, jpeg_sof, imagesize, orientation — and every one is a round-trip over SMB. The reply lands well after the user has clicked the next file. On a local disk it comes back in milliseconds, before the next click is physically possible, which is why this has never been seen locally.

The stale metadata is also what the metadata panel shows, so the same defect mislabels the panel for any file selected while a previous read is still in flight.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount an SMB share (e.g. as /Volumes/sambashare) holding both 360 images and a 360 (equirectangular) video.
  2. Open that folder in Preview.
  3. Click an image. Do not wait for the metadata panel to fill in.
  4. Click the 360 video.
  5. The video plays flat, and the toolbar shows only the flat button — no 360, no fisheye. The metadata panel still describes the image.

Same folder copied to a local disk: all three buttons appear, every time.

Goal

The metadata a file's view mode is derived from is that file's metadata, whatever the network latency.

Each reply is tagged with the path it answers, and the renderer accepts only its own:

  • msg_get_metadata echoes the requested file in all four of its emits (result and error, video and image path).
  • The listener ignores a reply for another file, and leaves it registered so the listener actually waiting on it can take it.
  • A reply that has been superseded by a newer selection stops waiting without overwriting the newer file's metadata. "Latest request" is tracked at module scope, since useSelectDisplay is instantiated by ~15 components and the latest selection is one global fact. Deselecting (selectDisplay(null), or picking a .pts) clears it, so a reply still in flight cannot repopulate an empty panel.

A fix along these lines is prepared on branch fix/nas, not yet committed. Verified only against a mounted SMB share plus pnpm typecheck / pnpm test / cargo check; wants a second pass on a slower share (WiFi) where the overlap window is wider.

Related, not fixed here

Video files never receive an asset-protocol scope grant. tauri.conf.json whitelists $HOME/** and friends only; /Volumes is widened at runtime by get_image_view (src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs), which grants the file and its parent directory. Images go through it; src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/useViewerImage.ts:89 takes displayedFile.url for videos and never calls it. A video in a share folder where no image has been opened yet is therefore served a 403 by the gtimg handler and renders black. Mixed folders hide this, because opening any image grants the whole directory.

issues.display_title: Issue #167: Creating a folder inside a mounted USB or network volume fails
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.59.21.mov

What happens

Creating a new folder inside a mounted USB or network volume fails. On macOS/Linux, create-folder prepends $HOME to the requested path unconditionally:

src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs — create_folder

let home = dirs::home_dir()...;
format!("{home}/{folder}")

The renderer sends the new folder as a display path, <currentDirectory>/<name> — for a share mounted at /Volumes/sambashare that is sambashare/Panorama/New folder. Prefixing home turns it into $HOME/sambashare/Panorama/New folder, whose parent does not exist, so the non-recursive create_dir fails with NotFound.

This is the same class of bug as #160 (copy/move into a mounted volume). That fix introduced the volumes-aware helper resolve_dest in the same file, but create_folder was never moved over to it — it is the only remaining hardcoded home_dir in fs_ops.rs.

Absolute paths are broken by the same line: /Volumes/x/y becomes $HOME//Volumes/x/y.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount an SMB share (e.g. as /Volumes/sambashare).
  2. In the app, navigate into the share — File Manager panel or Preview both reach this path.
  3. Create a new folder (toolbar button, context menu, or the app menu item).
  4. It fails. Nothing appears in the listing; the folder is not created on the share.

Compare with the same action inside a folder under $HOME, which works — that is the case the $HOME prefix was written for.

Goal

A new folder lands where the user asked, on a mounted volume as well as under home.

The fix is to route through the existing resolve_dest helper, but with one catch worth recording: resolve_dest distinguishes a home-relative display path from a mounted-volume one by testing which candidate exists. The folder being created never exists yet, so passing it the full path always loses that test and falls back to $HOME — the naive fix does not work. The parent has to be resolved, then the new name joined onto it:

let normalized = folder.replace('\\', "/");
let final_path = match normalized.rsplit_once('/') {
    Some((parent, name)) => resolve_dest(parent).join(name),
    None => resolve_dest(&normalized),
};

A fix along these lines, plus a regression test (create_folder_honours_a_path_outside_home, which creates a folder in a temp dir outside $HOME), is prepared on branch fix/nas but not yet committed or pushed. Needs verifying against a real share before it lands.

issues.display_title: Issue #170: Switching panoramas in Preview freezes the app on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Switching between panoramas in Preview on a network share freezes the app. Not on the first switch — it gets worse the longer the session runs, and eventually the window stops responding entirely. Three separate causes stack on the same code path.

1. Prefetch fans out to four neighbours in parallel, with no way to stop it

src/renderer/features/preview/ImageSphere.tsx:42-70 runs on every texture change and prefetches four surrounding files (before, after, prevTop, nextTop). Each one does:

  • getImageUrl(file) → get-image-view + get-image-size
  • useTexture.preload(url) → a full-resolution download over gtimg://

Nothing cancels an in-flight prefetch when the selection moves on. Arrowing through ten images leaves up to ~50 whole-file reads in flight at once. On a local disk this is invisible; on a share it saturates the link, fills the blocking pool, and every one of them holds an entire panorama in memory at the same time (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:190 — Vec::with_capacity(len) + read_to_end, tracked separately in #163).

2. Textures are never disposed

There is no dispose(), useTexture.clear() or THREE.Cache.remove anywhere in the renderer. drei's useTexture caches by URL in a global suspense cache and frees nothing, so every panorama ever displayed stays resident as a decoded bitmap plus a GPU texture. An 8000×4000 equirectangular is ~128 MB of VRAM. The setLoaded([0]) reset on directory change (ImageSphere.tsx:72-76) only resets React state — the cache survives it.

This is why the freeze is intermittent rather than immediate: it needs enough switches to exhaust memory.

3. get-image-size blocks an async-runtime worker

src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs:248 is async fn, but its body is fully blocking sync I/O with no spawn_blocking: imagesize::size, read_orientation and fs::metadata each open the file — three round-trips per file, multiplied by the prefetch fan-out. Same sweep as 5bfa5f1 and #168; this command was missed.

Contributing: the URL cache silently loses entries

src/renderer/hooks/useGetImage.tsx:69-72 writes setLoadedBlobUrl({ ...loadedBlobUrl, [path]: url }), spreading a copy captured in the closure. The displayed panorama and its prefetched neighbours resolve concurrently, so whichever lands last drops the others' entries. The cache keeps missing and the same files are fetched again on the next switch. fileDimensions already has mergeFileDimensions for exactly this reason; loadedBlobUrl never got the equivalent.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a slow network share (SMB over a VPN/tunnel makes it obvious).
  2. Open a folder of full-resolution equirectangular panoramas from that share in Preview.
  3. Hold the right arrow key, or click through 15–30 panoramas at a normal browsing pace.
  4. The window stalls for progressively longer between images, then stops responding.

Watching memory during step 3 shows it climbing and never coming back down. The stall does not clear by waiting — only by restarting.

Goal

  1. Switching panoramas on a network share stays responsive, and stays responsive for the length of a browsing session rather than degrading.
  2. The number of concurrent full-resolution reads is bounded and does not scale with how fast the user is switching. A prefetch for an image the user has already moved past must not keep running.
  3. Texture memory is bounded. A texture that falls out of the working set is disposed; a texture still bound to the sphere never is (disposing that one renders it black).
  4. Prefetching still earns its keep: stepping to the next or previous image on a slow share should be near-instant, and stepping back to one just visited must not re-download it.
  5. The visible panorama loads before any prefetch starts — a prefetch must never delay the image the user actually asked for.
  6. Existing behaviour is unchanged: the loading overlay in PanoramaViewer.tsx, the progress bar in PanoramaLoader.tsx, the error modal from useViewerImage, and flat/little-planet/video view modes.
